title: Five black keys, two pianists
work: Étude in G♭ major, Op. 10 No. 5
question: How much of this étude’s wit comes from the left hand beneath those racing black-key runs?
intro: Chopin sends the right hand racing over the five black keys, with detached chords and octaves underneath. A loud phrase comes back as a quiet answer; even at speed, the piano seems to be talking to itself. Cortot and Neeman carry this two-handed conversation to a final dash in octaves.

recordings.label: Edward Neeman
recordings.note: Neeman’s Chopin recordings include the complete études and thirty-one mazurkas; he also plays piano duets with his wife, Stephanie.

recordings.label: Alfred Cortot, 1920
recordings.note: Cortot’s teaching edition treats this étude as a lesson in supple hand movement and a brilliant, delicately connected touch.

passages.label: A bold phrase, a quiet answer
passages.note: The right-hand triplets skim over detached left-hand chords; loud phrases find quick, quiet answers.

passages.label: The phrase stretches into D♭
passages.note: The triplets carry on in D♭ major as the left hand stretches the phrase beyond the opening’s neat four-bar groups.

passages.label: The opening returns
passages.note: The opening figure returns in G♭ major, then begins to soften towards a passage marked very delicate and dying away.

passages.label: Both hands join the dash
passages.note: Wide arpeggios spread across the keyboard before both hands finish in a rapid, detached run of black-key octaves.
